headings: Present Position and Other Position(s) Held During Last Five Years
paragraphs: PACCAR Inc (the Company or PACCAR), incorporated under the laws of Delaware in 1971, is the successor to Pacific Car and Foundry Company which was incorporated in Washington in 1924. The Company traces its predecessors to Seattle Car Manufacturing Company formed in 1905.
PACCAR is a multinational company operating in three principal industry segments:

(1) The Truck segment includes the design, manufacture and distribution of high-quality, light-, medium- and heavy-duty commercial trucks. Heavy-duty trucks have a gross vehicle weight (GVW) of over 33,000 lbs (Class 8) in North America and over 16 metric tonnes in Europe and South America. Medium-duty trucks have a GVW ranging from 19,500 to 33,000 lbs (Class 6 to 7) in North America, and in Europe, light- and medium-duty trucks range between 6 and 16 metric tonnes. Trucks are configured with the engine in front of cab (conventional) or cab-over-engine (COE).
(2) The Parts segment includes the distribution of aftermarket parts for trucks and related commercial vehicles.

(3) The Financial Services segment includes finance and leasing products and services provided to customers and dealers. PACCAR's finance and leasing activities are principally related to PACCAR products and associated equipment.

PACCAR's trucks are marketed under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates. These trucks, which are built in three plants in the United States, three in Europe and one each in Australia, Brasil, Canada and Mexico, are used worldwide for over-the-road and off-highway hauling of commercial and consumer goods. The Company also designs and manufactures diesel engines, primarily for use in the Company's trucks, at its facilities in Columbus, Mississippi; Eindhoven, the Netherlands and Ponta Grossa, Brasil. PACCAR competes in the North American Class 8 market, primarily with Kenworth and Peterbilt conventional models. These trucks are assembled at facilities in Chillicothe, Ohio; Denton, Texas; Renton, Washington; Mexicali, Mexico and Ste. Therese, Canada. PACCAR also competes in the North American Class 6 to 7 markets primarily with Kenworth and Peterbilt conventional models. These trucks are assembled at facilities in Ste. Therese, Canada; Chillicothe, Ohio; Denton, Texas and Mexicali, Mexico. PACCAR competes in the European light/medium market with DAF COE trucks assembled in the United Kingdom (U.K.) by Leyland, one of PACCAR's wholly owned subsidiaries, and participates in the European heavy market with DAF COE trucks assembled in the Netherlands and the U.K. PACCAR competes in the Brazilian heavy truck market with DAF COE models assembled in Ponta Grossa in the state of Paraná, Brasil. PACCAR competes in the Australian medium and heavy truck markets with Kenworth conventional and COE models and certain DAF COE models assembled at its facility at Bayswater in the state of Victoria, Australia, and DAF COE models primarily assembled in the U.K. Commercial truck manufacturing comprises the largest segment of PACCAR's business and accounted for 68% of total 2025 net sales and revenues.

Substantially all trucks are sold to independent dealers. The Kenworth and Peterbilt nameplates are marketed and distributed by separate divisions in the U.S. and a foreign subsidiary in Canada. The Kenworth nameplate is also marketed and distributed by foreign subsidiaries in Mexico and Australia. The DAF nameplate is marketed and distributed worldwide by a foreign subsidiary headquartered in the Netherlands and is also marketed and distributed by foreign subsidiaries in Brasil, Australia and Mexico. The decision to operate as a subsidiary or as a division is incidental to PACCAR's Truck segment operations and reflects legal, tax and regulatory requirements in the various countries where PACCAR operates.

The Truck segment utilizes centrally managed purchasing, information technology, technical research and testing, treasury and finance functions. Some manufacturing plants in North America produce trucks for more than one nameplate, while other plants produce trucks for only one nameplate, depending on various factors. Best manufacturing practices within the Company are shared on a routine basis reflecting the similarity of the business models employed by each nameplate.

The Company's trucks have a reputation for high quality products, most of which are ordered by dealers according to customer specifications. Some units are ordered by dealers for stocking to meet the needs of certain customers who require immediate delivery or for customers that require the chassis to be fitted with specialized bodies. For a significant portion of the Company's truck operations, major components, such as engines, transmissions and axles, as well as a substantial percentage of other components, are purchased from component manufacturers pursuant to PACCAR and customer specifications. DAF, which is more vertically integrated, manufactures PACCAR engines and axles and a higher percentage of other components for its heavy truck models. The Company also manufactures engines at its Columbus, Mississippi facility. In 2025, the Company installed PACCAR engines in approximately 29% of the Company's Kenworth and Peterbilt heavy-duty trucks in the U.S. and Canada and substantially all of the DAF heavy-duty trucks sold throughout the world. Engines not manufactured by the Company are purchased from Cummins Inc. (Cummins). The Company purchased a significant portion of its transmissions from Eaton Corporation Plc. (Eaton) and ZF Friedrichshafen AG (ZF). The Company also purchased a significant portion of North America stampings used for cabs from Magna International Inc. (Magna). The Company has long-term agreements with Cummins, Eaton, ZF and Magna to provide for continuity of supply. A loss of supply from Cummins, Eaton, ZF or Magna, and the resulting interruption in the production of trucks, would have a material effect on the Company's results. Purchased materials and parts include raw materials, partially processed materials, such as castings, and finished components manufactured by independent suppliers. The Company and its suppliers rely on semiconductors as an essential component in the production of its trucks and aftermarket parts. The Company and its suppliers source semiconductors from various suppliers. Raw materials, partially processed materials and finished components typically make up approximately 85% of the cost of new trucks. The value of finished truck components manufactured by independent suppliers is lower in Europe due to a higher level of vertical integration as compared to North America. In addition to materials, the Company's cost of sales includes labor and factory overhead, vehicle delivery and warranty. Accordingly, except for certain factory overhead costs such as facilities depreciation, property taxes and utilities, the Company's cost of sales are highly correlated to sales.

The Company's DAF subsidiary purchases fully assembled cabs from a competitor, Renault V.I., for its European light-, medium-duty product line pursuant to a joint product development and long-term supply contract. Sales of trucks manufactured with these cabs amounted to approximately 2% of consolidated revenues in 2025. A short-term loss of supply, and the resulting interruption in the production of these trucks, would not have a material effect on the Company's results of operations. However, a loss of supply for an extended period of time would require the Company to either contract for an alternative source of supply or to manufacture cabs itself.

Other than these components, the Company is not limited to any single source for any significant component, although the sudden inability of a supplier to deliver components could have a temporary adverse effect on production of certain products. Manufacturing inventory levels are based upon production schedules and orders are placed with suppliers accordingly.

Key factors affecting Truck segment earnings include the number of new trucks sold in the markets served and the margins realized on the sales. The Company's sales of new trucks are dependent on the size of the truck markets served and the Company's share of those markets. Truck segment sales and margins tend to be cyclical based on the level of overall economic activity, the availability of capital and the amount of freight being transported. The Company's costs for trucks consist primarily of material costs, which are influenced by the price of commodities such as steel, copper, aluminum and petroleum. The Company utilizes long-term supply agreements to reduce the variability of the unit cost of purchased materials and finished components and engages in hedging activities for some commodities in certain geographical markets. The Company's spending on research and development varies based on product development cycles and government requirements such as changes to diesel engine emissions and vehicle fuel efficiency standards in the various markets served. The Company maintains rigorous control of selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses and seeks to minimize such costs.

There are four principal competitors in the U.S. and Canada commercial truck market. The Company's share of the U.S. and Canadian Class 8 market was 29.9% of retail sales in 2025, and the Company's medium-duty market share was 15.9%. In Europe, there are six principal competitors in the commercial truck market, including parent companies to the four competitors of the Company in the U.S. In 2025, DAF had a 13.5% share of the European heavy-duty market and a 9.7% share of the light/medium-duty market. These markets are highly competitive in price, quality and service. PACCAR is not dependent on any single customer for its sales. There are no significant seasonal variations in sales.

The Peterbilt, Kenworth and DAF nameplates are recognized internationally and play an important role in the marketing of the Company's truck products. The Company engages in a continuous program of trademark and trade name protection in all marketing areas of the world.
The following are significant risks which could have a material negative impact on the Company's financial condition or results of operations.

Commercial Truck Market Demand is Variable. The Company's business is highly sensitive to global and national economic conditions as well as economic conditions in the industries and markets it serves. Negative economic conditions and outlook can materially weaken demand for the Company's equipment and services. The yearly demand for commercial vehicles may increase or decrease more than overall gross domestic product in markets the Company serves, which are principally North America and Europe. Demand for commercial vehicles may also be affected by the introduction of new vehicles and technologies by the Company or its competitors.

Competition and Prices. The Company operates in a highly competitive environment, which could adversely affect the Company's sales and pricing. Financial results depend largely on the ability to develop, manufacture and market competitive products that profitably meet customer demand.

Production Costs, Capacity and Inflation. The Company's products are exposed to variability in material and commodity costs. Commodity or component price increases, cost pressures due to inflation, significant shortages of component products and labor availability may adversely impact the Company's financial results or use of its production capacity. Many of the Company's suppliers also supply automotive manufacturers, and factors that adversely affect the automotive industry can also have adverse effects on these suppliers and the Company. Supplier delivery performance can be adversely affected if increased demand for these suppliers' products exceeds their production capacity.

Unexpected events, including natural disasters, extreme weather events, or pandemics, may increase the Company's cost of doing business or disrupt the Company's or its suppliers' operations. The likelihood or severity of these unexpected events may increase due to the effects of climate change.

Transition Risks Related to Climate Change. The Company has ongoing product development programs intended to address changing customer demand in the context of climate change and achieve its targeted reductions in emissions. These involve the continuing development of compliant clean diesel powertrains and the design, manufacture, and sale of alternative powertrain commercial vehicles (e.g., battery-electric, hybrid, hydrogen fuel cell, and hydrogen combustion). paragraphs: PACCAR is a global technology company whose Truck segment includes the design and manufacture of high-quality light-, medium- and heavy-duty commercial trucks. In the U.S. and Canada, trucks are sold under the Kenworth and Peterbilt nameplates, in Europe, under the DAF nameplate and in Mexico, Australia and South America, under the Kenworth and DAF nameplates. The Parts segment includes the distribution of aftermarket parts for trucks and related commercial vehicles. The Company's Financial Services segment derives its earnings primarily from financing or leasing PACCAR products in North America, Europe, Australia and South America.

• Worldwide net sales and revenues were $28.44 billion in 2025 compared to $33.66 billion in 2024, primarily due to lower truck revenues, partially offset by higher parts and financial services revenues.
• Truck sales were $19.37 billion in 2025 compared to $24.84 billion in 2024 due to lower truck deliveries in all major markets.
• Parts sales were $6.87 billion in 2025 compared to $6.67 billion in 2024, reflecting higher sales in the U.S. and Canada
• Financial Services revenues were $2.21 billion in 2025 compared to $2.10 billion in 2024, primarily due to higher interest income driven by retail portfolio growth and higher portfolio yields.
• In 2025, PACCAR earned net income for the 87th consecutive year. Net income was $2.38 billion ($4.51 per diluted share) in 2025 compared to $4.16 billion ($7.90 per diluted share) in 2024.

• Adjusted net income (non-GAAP), excluding a $264.5 million after-tax charge related to civil litigation in Europe, was $2.64 billion ($5.01 per diluted share). After-tax return on beginning equity (ROE) was 13.6% in 2025, which includes the $264.5 million after-tax charge related to civil litigation in Europe in the first quarter of this year. Excluding the after-tax charge, adjusted ROE (non-GAAP) was 15.1%. This compares to an ROE of 26.2% in 2024. See Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Financial Measures on page 31.
• Capital investments were $728.5 million in 2025 compared to $795.8 million in 2024.
• Research and development (R&D) expenses were $445.5 million in 2025 compared to $452.9 million in 2024.

Kenworth constructed a 46,000 square-foot robotic chassis paint facility in Chillicothe, Ohio. PACCAR also completed a new $35 million, 50,000 square-foot engine remanufacturing facility and is enhancing its existing engine factory in Columbus, Mississippi. PACCAR is also enhancing its other engine facility in the Netherlands. PACCAR opened a new 180,000 square-foot Parts Distribution Center (PDC) in Calgary, Canada, to enhance parts delivery to dealers and customers in the region.

The PACCAR Financial Services (PFS) group of companies has operations covering four continents and 26 countries. The global breadth of PFS and its rigorous credit application process support a portfolio of loans and leases with total assets of $22.80 billion. PFS issued $3.12 billion in medium-term notes during 2025 to support new business volume and market share growth and repay maturing debt.

Truck industry heavy-duty retail sales in the U.S. and Canada in 2026 are expected to be 230,000 to 270,000 units compared to 232,800 in 2025. In Europe, the 2026 truck industry registrations for over 16-tonne vehicles are expected to be 280,000 to 320,000 units compared to 297,000 in 2025. In South America, heavy-duty truck industry registrations in 2026 are projected to be 100,000 to 110,000 compared to 115,000 in 2025.

The Company's truck and parts products have been negatively affected since March 2025 by import tariffs imposed by the U.S. government and actions taken by other countries. While the Company has taken mitigating actions to reduce the impact, the ongoing impact from import tariffs on truck order intake and profit margins remains unfavorable. The Company's North American truck factories are optimally located to operate under the new Section 232 truck tariffs that began in November 2025. The Company's tariff exposure is minimized by producing trucks locally for the United States, Canada and Mexico. The Company manufactures its trucks for U.S. customers in its Ohio, Texas, and Washington state factories.

The recent U.S. Environmental Protection Agency announcement reaffirmed the EPA27 NOx limit and could eliminate changes to extended warranty requirements and useful life requirements on new emissions systems. The Company's results could be impacted by changes in tariff policy, including the expected U.S. Supreme Court ruling on the International Emergency Economic Power Acts (IEEPA) tariffs, emissions regulations and improving freight fundamentals.

headings: 現任職務及其他於最近五年內所擔任之職務
paragraphs: PACCAR Inc (the Company or PACCAR), 依照德拉瓦州法律設立於1971年，為太平洋汽車與鑄造公司之繼承者，該公司於華盛頓州設立於1924年。the Company 之前身可追溯至1905年成立之西雅圖汽車製造公司。
PACCAR 為一跨國公司，經營三大主要產業分部：
(1) 汽車分部包括設計、製造與分銷高品質之輕型、中型及重型商用貨車。重型貨車在北美地區之總重量超過33,000磅（Class 8），在歐洲與南美洲地區則超過16公噸。中型貨車在北美地區總重量範圍為19,500至33,000磅（Class 6至7），在歐洲地區，輕型與中型貨車總重量範圍為6至16公噸。貨車配置方式為引擎位於駕駛室前方（傳統式）或駕駛室位於引擎上方（COE）。
(2) 配件分部包括分銷商用貨車及相關商用車之後市場零組件。
(3) 金融服務分部包括提供予客戶與經銷商之融資與租賃產品與服務。PACCAR 之融資與租賃業務主要與 PACCAR 產品及相關設備有關。

PACCAR 之貨車以 Kenworth、Peterbilt 及 DAF 名稱銷售。這些貨車於美國三座工廠、歐洲三座工廠，以及澳洲、巴西、加拿大與墨西哥各一座工廠製造，廣泛用於全球公路與非公路運輸商業與消費商品。the Company 亦設計與製造柴油引擎，主要用於本公司貨車，於密蘇裏州哥倫布市、荷蘭埃因霍溫及巴西龐塔格羅薩設有廠區。PACCAR 在北美 Class 8 市場與 Kenworth 及 Peterbilt 之傳統式貨車競爭。這些貨車於俄亥俄州奇利科特、德克薩斯州登頓、華盛頓州雷nton、墨西哥墨西卡利及加拿大聖泰蕾絲工廠組裝。PACCAR 也在北美 Class 6 至 7 市場與 Kenworth 及 Peterbilt 之傳統式貨車競爭。這些貨車於加拿大聖泰蕾絲、俄亥俄州奇利科特、德克薩斯州登頓及墨西哥墨西卡利工廠組裝。PACCAR 在歐洲輕型/中型市場與由 PACCAR 之 wholly owned 子公司 Leyland 在英國（U.K.）組裝之 DAF COE 貨車競爭，並在歐洲重型市場參與與於荷蘭及英國組裝之 DAF COE 貨車競爭。PACCAR 在巴西重型貨車市場與於巴西巴拉那州龐塔格羅薩組裝之 DAF COE 貨車競爭。PACCAR 在澳洲中型及重型貨車市場與於澳洲維多利亞州拜斯沃特工廠組裝之 Kenworth 傳統式及 COE 貨車及部分 DAF COE 貨車競爭，並與於英國組裝之 DAF COE 貨車競爭。商用貨車製造為 PACCAR 之最大業務分部，佔2025年總淨銷售額與營業收入之68%。

幾乎所有貨車均銷售予獨立經銷商。Kenworth 與 Peterbilt 名稱於美國由獨立部門行銷與分銷，並於加拿大之外資子公司行銷與分銷。Kenworth 名稱亦於墨西哥與澳洲之外資子公司行銷與分銷。DAF 名稱由於荷蘭設立之外資子公司全球行銷與分銷，並於巴西、澳洲與墨西哥設有外資子公司行銷與分銷。以子公司或部門形式運作之決定與 PACCAR 之 Truck 分部運作無關，並反映於 PACCAR 營運之各國法律、稅務與法規要求。
Truck 分部運用中央管理之採購、資訊科技、技術研究與測試、財務與會計功能。北美部分製造工廠生產多個品牌之貨車，而其他工廠則僅生產單一品牌之貨車，視各項因素而定。the Company 會定期分享最佳製造實踐，反映各品牌所採用之業務模式相似性。

本公司的卡車以高品質產品聞名，大多數產品是經銷商根據客戶規格訂購的。部分單位是經銷商為庫存而訂購，以應對某些需要立即交貨的客戶或需要車架安裝特殊車身的客戶。對於本公司卡車業務的大部分運作，主要零組件，如引擎、變速箱和軸承，以及大量其他零組件，是根據 PACCAR 和客戶規格向零組件製造商購入。DAF 由於更垂直整合，製造 PACCAR 引擎和軸承，以及更高比例的其他零組件用於其重型卡車模型。本公司也在密西西比州哥倫布市製造引擎。2025 年，本公司在美國和加拿大約 29% 的 Kenworth 和 Peterbilt 重型卡車安裝了 PACCAR 引擎，並在全世界幾乎所有 DAF 重型卡車中使用。未由本公司製造的引擎則向 Cummins Inc. (Cummins) 購買。本公司從 Eaton Corporation Plc. (Eaton) 和 ZF Friedrichshafen AG (ZF) 購買了大量變速箱。本公司也從 Magna International Inc. (Magna) 購買了北美用於駕駛室的大量衝壓件。本公司與 Cummins、Eaton、ZF 和 Magna 籤訂了長期協議，以確保供應的連續性。若 Cummins、Eaton、ZF 或 Magna 的供應中斷，導致卡車生產中斷，將對本公司結果產生重大影響。購入的材料和零件包括原材料、部分加工材料，如鑄造件，以及由獨立供應商製造的成品零組件。本公司及其供應商依賴半導體作為生產卡車和後市場零件的關鍵零組件。本公司及其供應商從多個供應商處取得半導體。原材料、部分加工材料和成品零組件通常佔新卡車成本的約 85%。由於歐洲垂直整合程度較高，由獨立供應商製造的成品卡車零組件價值較低。除了材料外，本公司銷售成本還包括人工、工廠間接費用、車輛交付及保証費用。因此，除了某些工廠間接費用如廠房折舊、不動產稅及電力費用外，本公司銷售成本與銷售額高度相關。
本公司的 DAF 子公司根據一項聯合產品開發和長期供應契約，從競爭對手 Renault V.I. 購買完全組裝的駕駛室，用於其歐洲輕型及中型卡車產品線。使用這些駕駛室製造的卡車銷售額在 2025 年約佔合併營收的 2%。短期供應中斷，導致這些卡車生產中斷，不會對本公司營運結果產生重大影響。然而，若供應中斷時間過長，本公司將需要尋找替代供應來源或自行製造駕駛室。
除了這些零組件外，本公司並未對任何重要零組件依賴單一來源，雖然供應商突然無法交貨可能對某些產品的生產產生暫時的負面影響。製造存貨水平是根據生產排程及訂單向供應商下達。

影響卡車業務獲利的主要因素包括在所服務市場銷售的新卡車數量以及銷售所實現的毛利率。本公司銷售新卡車取決於所服務市場的規模以及本公司在這些市場的佔有率。卡車業務銷售和毛利率通常具有週期性，取決於總體經濟活動水平、資金可得性以及運輸貨物的數量。本公司卡車的成本主要為材料成本，受鋼鐵、銅、鋁和石油等商品價格影響。本公司利用長期供應契約來降低購入材料和成品零組件的單位成本變動，並在某些地理市場對部分商品進行對沖活動。本公司在研究與開發上的支出會根據產品開發週期及政府要求，如各市場柴油引擎排放標準和車輛燃油效率標準的變更而有所不同。本公司嚴格控制銷售、一般及行政費用 (SG&A)，並致力於降低這些費用。

美國和加拿大商業卡車市場有四家主要競爭對手。本公司在 2025 年美國和加拿大 Class 8 市場的零售銷售佔有率為 29.9%，中型卡車市場佔有率為 15.9%。在歐洲，商業卡車市場有六家主要競爭對手，包括本公司在美國的四家競爭對手的母公司。2025 年，DAF 在歐洲重型卡車市場佔有率為 13.5%，在輕型/中型卡車市場佔有率為 9.7%。這些市場在價格、品質和服務方面競爭激烈。PACCAR 不依賴任何單一客戶進行銷售。銷售無顯著季節性變動。
Peterbilt、Kenworth 和 DAF 的品牌在國際上被認可，並在本公司卡車產品的行銷中扮演重要角色。本公司在全球各行銷領域持續進行商標和商標名稱的保護工作。

paragraphs: PACCAR 為一全球性科技公司，其貨車分部包括設計與製造高品質的輕型、中型及重型商用貨車。在美國與加拿大，貨車以 Kenworth 與 Peterbilt 品牌銷售；在歐洲，以 DAF 品牌銷售；在墨西哥、澳洲與南美洲，則以 Kenworth 與 DAF 品牌銷售。零組件分部包括後市場零組件與相關商用車輛的分銷。本公司財務服務分部的獲利主要來自於北美、歐洲、澳洲與南美洲的 PACCAR 產品融資或租賃業務。
• 全球淨銷售額與營業收入為 2025 年 284.4 億美元，較 2024 年 336.6 億美元減少，主要因貨車收入減少，部分抵銷因零組件與財務服務收入增加的影響。
• 貨車銷售為 2025 年 193.7 億美元，較 2024 年 248.4 億美元減少，因所有主要市場的貨車交付量減少。
• 零組件銷售為 2025 年 68.7 億美元，較 2024 年 66.7 億美元增加，反映美國與加拿大銷售增加。
• 財務服務收入為 2025 年 22.1 億美元，較 2024 年 21 億美元增加，主要因零售投資組合成長與投資組合收益率提高所導致的利息收入增加。
• 2025 年，PACCAR 連續第 87 年獲取淨利潤。2025 年淨利潤為 238 億美元（每股稀釋後 4.51 美元），較 2024 年 416 億美元（每股稀釋後 7.90 美元）減少。

• 調整後淨利潤（非 GAAP），扣除歐洲民事訴訟相關 26.45 億美元稅後賠損後為 264 億美元（每股稀釋後 5.01 美元）。2025 年稅後權益報酬率（ROE）為 13.6%，包含 2025 年第一季因民事訴訟相關 26.45 億美元稅後賠損。扣除稅後賠損後，調整後 ROE（非 GAAP）為 15.1%。與 2024 年 ROE 為 26.2% 相較。請參閱第 31 頁「GAAP 與非 GAAP 財務指標的對應說明」。
• 2025 年資本投資為 72.85 億美元，較 2024 年 79.58 億美元減少。
• 研發費用（R&D expenses）於2025年為4.455億美元，較2024年的4.529億美元減少。

Kenworth 在俄亥俄州奇利科西建造了一座46,000平方英尺的機械骨架噴漆工廠。PACCAR 也完成了價值3500萬美元、50,000平方英尺的新引擎再製造工廠，並正在增強其位於密西西比州哥倫布的現有引擎工廠。PACCAR 同時也在荷蘭增強其其他引擎工廠。PACCAR 在加拿大卡爾加利開設了一座新180,000平方英尺的零件配送中心（Parts Distribution Center, PDC），以提升該地區經銷商與客戶的零件配送效率。
PACCAR 財務服務（PACCAR Financial Services, PFS）集團公司在四大洲、26個國家設有業務。PFS 的全球規模與嚴謹的信用申請程序，支持其貸款與租賃組合的總資產為228億美元。PFS 於2025年發行了312億美元的中期票據，以支持新業務量與市場佔有率的成長，並償還到期債務。
美國與加拿大2026年重型貨車零售銷售預計為23萬至27萬輛，較2025年的232,800輛有所減少。在歐洲，2026年超過16噸貨車的登記數預計為28萬至32萬輛，較2025年的297,000輛有所減少。在南美洲，2026年重型貨車的登記數預計為10萬至11萬輛，較2025年的115,000輛有所減少。

自2025年3月起，本公司貨車與零件產品因美國政府課徵的進口關稅及其他國家的措施而受到負面影響。雖然本公司已採取緩衝措施以降低影響，但進口關稅對貨車訂單與毛利的持續影響仍為不利因素。本公司北美貨車工廠的設置已最佳化，以在2025年11月開始實施的第232條款貨車關稅下運作。本公司透過在美國、加拿大與墨西哥本地生產貨車，以降低關稅風險。本公司在俄亥俄州、德克薩斯州與華盛頓州的工廠為美國客戶製造貨車。
美國環保署（EPA）最近的公告重申了EPA27 NOx 排放限制，可能消除對新排放系統延長保固與使用壽命要求的變更。本公司結果可能受到關稅政策變更的影響，包括預期美國最高法院對國際緊急經濟權力法案（International Emergency Economic Power Acts, IEEPA）關稅、排放規範及貨運基本面改善的裁決。
下列為可能對本公司財務狀況或營運成果造成重大負面影響的重要風險。
商用卡車市場需求具有變動性。本公司業務高度依賴全球及國家經濟狀況，以及其所服務產業與市場的經濟狀況。負面經濟狀況與預期可能顯著降低本公司設備與服務的需求。本公司所服務市場中，商用車輛的年度需求可能增加或減少幅度超過該市場總體經濟的成長率，這些市場主要為北美與歐洲。商用車輛的需求也可能受到本公司或其競爭對手推出新車型與技術的影響。
競爭與價格。本公司營運於高度競爭的環境中，這可能會對本公司銷售與價格造成不利影響。財務表現 largely 依賴開發、製造與行銷具競爭力的產品，以符合客戶需求並獲取利潤的能力。
生產成本、產能與通貨膨脹。本公司產品會受到原材料與商品成本變動的影響。商品或零組件價格上漲、通貨膨脹所導致的成本壓力、零組件產品的重大短缺以及勞動力可得性，可能會對本公司財務表現或生產能力的使用造成不利影響。許多本公司供應商同時也供應汽車製造商，因此影響汽車產業的不利因素，也可能對這些供應商與本公司造成不利影響。若這些供應商產品的需求增加超過其生產能力，則其交貨表現可能會受到不利影響。
未預期事件，包括天然災害、極端天氣事件或疫情，可能會提高本公司營運成本或幹擾本公司或其供應商的營運。這些未預期事件的發生機率或嚴重程度，可能因氣候變遷的影響而增加。
與氣候變遷相關的轉型風險。本公司持續進行產品開發計畫，以因應氣候變遷下客戶需求的變化，並實現其減排目標。這些計畫包括持續開發符合規範的潔淨柴油動力系統，以及設計、製造與銷售替代動力系統的商用車輛（例如電動車、混合動力車、氫燃料電池車與氫燃燒車）。從柴油燃燒轉型至替代動力系統商用車輛的轉型速度極為不確定，並會受到以下因素的影響：
